Noah (Design): quick discovery from the accessibility pass: Cmd+K shortcut that focuses the topbar search conflicts with browser find on some setups and VoiceOver announces the search twice on open. Also people reported that when suggestions load there's no concise announcement of counts. Repro: Cmd+K -> focus goes to input, VO says 'Search' then 'Search' again, and when typing 'red' suggestions show but VO doesn't say '3 suggestions'. Link to prototype: https://figma.redwood.app/topbar-shortcuts Aria (Frontend): I can repro on my Mac. DOM seems to have a visible label + sr-only text + aria-label on the input. The shortcut handler calls input.focus() and then we programmatically set aria-live to describe the initial state which may cause duplicate speaks. Also Cmd+K is registered globally and some browsers intercept it for quick find. Dee (A11y): a few separate issues: 1) Accessible name collision -> multiple name sources (label + aria-label + sr-only) cause double announce. Pick one source. Prefer label + aria-labelledby or sr-only label, not aria-label + visible label. 2) Programmatic focus + immediate aria-live announcement can double speak: when focus lands, the screen reader will announce the control name; then aria-live speaking the same phrase duplicates. Instead, defer aria-live summary until after focus settles and don't repeat the control name. 3) For suggestions, use a polite aria-live message like '3 suggestions' when the list appears, and use listbox/option semantics so arrowing announces the active option. 4) Shortcuts: expose the shortcut in the accessible name (e.g., 'Search (press K)') is okay visually, but don't intercept modifier combos that a browser might use. We can keep Cmd/Control+K and add ALT+S as a fallback for Windows browsers where Ctrl/Cmd+K conflicts. Noah (Design): good. UX question: do we want the aria-live summary to read only counts or also the type (e.g., '3 suggestions for "red"')? Too verbose might be noisy. Rex (QA): from testing, concise is better: '3 suggestions for red' is fine if it's one-shot when list appears. It shouldn't speak on every keystroke. Also ensure NVDA/JAWS behavior on Windows (Firefox/Chrome) is consistent. Aria (Frontend): proposed implementation plan: - Use a single source of accessible name: keep visible and input aria-labelledby="search-label". Remove aria-label on input. - Add an sr-only span inside the label for SR context: Search Redwood Console while visually showing "Search" only. - When opening suggestions, set #search-status (aria-live="polite") to "3 suggestions for \"red\"" after a 250ms debounce (not on every keystroke). Do not include the control name in this message. - Convert suggestions to role="listbox"/role="option" and use aria-activedescendant on the input while keeping focus on the input (don't move focus). - Shortcuts: keep Cmd/Ctrl+K but add Alt+S for Windows and expose the available shortcuts in the cheat sheet (accessible from Help). Also, when shortcut is triggered, push a concise sr-only hint to the status: "Search focused, type to find models". Code example to avoid duplicate announce: ```
  • Redwood
    • ...
``` And JS: ``` // on suggestions update (debounced) statusEl.textContent = `${count} suggestions for "${query}"`; // avoid status update when focus first lands (focus handler sets a flag) ``` Dee (A11y): that looks good. Two more nits: 1) When programmatically focusing via shortcut, set a short delay before writing to status so the SR will first announce the control and then the status; 2) prefer role="status" with aria-live="polite" for one-off updates. Also ensure we don't rely on CSS-only hiding for the sr-only content; use established sr-only utility that keeps content in accessibility tree. Noah (Design): about focus ring contrast on keyboard focus when invoked via shortcut: a few participants flagged it's subtle in dark theme. Can we increase ring thickness or add a faint halo? Keep consistent with other components. Aria (Frontend): will bump focus-visible for the input and for active listbox option for dark theme. Example CSS: ``` #search-input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--blue-400); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(96,165,250,0.09); } [role="option"]:focus-visible, [role="option"].active { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px rgba(96,165,250,0.14); } ``` Rex (QA): test plan: add keyboard-only flows for both shortcuts (Cmd/Ctrl+K and Alt+S), verify single announce on focus, verify status message appears once per suggestion-render (debounced), verify listbox semantics announce active option on arrow, and visual snapshot of focus ring in light/dark. I'll run on macOS (VO/Safari), Windows (NVDA/Firefox, JAWS/Chrome). Dee (A11y): I'll review the PR and run cross-platform checks. If we see inconsistent announce timing, we can tweak the 250ms debounce or change to manual announcements after aria-activedescendant changes. Noah (Design): owners: Aria (impl), Dee (a11y review), Rex (QA). Target: patch release this sprint. search-bot: updated shortcut docs (https://docs.redwood.ai/shortcuts) :wrench:
